title: Cross-border transmission can reach commercial operation before household affordability is visible
source_unit: NYSERDA and New York State announcement of commercial operation of the Champlain Hudson Power Express transmission project
geography: Quebec, Canada; New York State; New York City Zone J

observations.period: June 16, 2026 announcement; commercial operation reported May 13, 2026

physical_delivery.unit: terawatt-hours of clean energy expected per year delivered into the New York metro area

system_reach.unit: percent of New York City's energy needs the project is expected to meet

cross_border_dependency.value: Hydro-Québec power delivered through a 339-mile transmission line into NYISO Zone J

public_claims.value: 37 million metric tons of carbon emissions expected to be reduced through 2040 and more than 1,400 construction and operations jobs supported
public_claims.unit: reported projected public and labor effects

household_bill_effect_and_local_acceptan.unit: missing customer-level bill, affordability, reliability, burden, and durable acceptance outcome

observations.method: Official NYSERDA/New York State project announcement and NYSERDA Tier Four program page; commercial operation, delivered-energy route, cross-border dependency, and projected public effects are coded separately from realized household bills, rate allocation, reliability, and acceptance.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement reports commercial operation and expected annual delivery, but does not provide customer-level bill changes, rate-class allocation, actual monthly delivery series, reliability outcomes, project cost incidence, or later public acceptance. The public-health and emissions figures are projections or modeled effects rather than person-level outcomes.
observations.subgroup: New York City and New York State electricity customers, communities along the route, Hydro-Québec and New York system operators, construction and operations workers, and communities described as disadvantaged; subgroup-level realized effects are not reported.
observations.counterinterpretation: A cross-border project can create real operating capacity and reduce emissions while its costs, benefits, and reliability effects are distributed unevenly. Commercial operation does not show that a household received cheaper or more reliable service, or that host communities accepted the project over time.

related_sources.claim: New York load-serving entities have a 2026 obligation tied to Tier 4 renewable energy certificates delivered through the project into NYISO Zone J.
related_sources.access_boundary: The obligation and delivered-energy accounting route do not establish a household bill change or individual receipt.

boundary: This record establishes a cross-border infrastructure project reaching commercial operation and a reported route for clean electricity delivery into New York. It does not establish realized household affordability, customer-class allocation, reliability improvement, host-community acceptance, or durable geopolitical leverage. It is an infrastructure and state-dependence realization case, not a household benefit estimate.
